594.t: Cafe Wha? sessions and being hired by Mingus
594.s: At Greenwich Village jam sessions, Mingus needed alto and trumpet players, heard McPherson and Hillyer, and hired them alongside the departing Eric Dolphy.
594.q: Well I knew him as Noel. Oh, okay. All right. Now he was just a folk singer singing, playing his guitar, and then we had this jam session in the afternoon, and Bill Cosby or people like that or even Bob Dylan would be at some coffee house across the street, and everybody was just like struggling…

594.s: Mingus's music was hard to interpret, he was never satisfied, and he thrived on tension and theatrics.
594.q: Yeah he wrote things out and some things he didn’t write out. It didn’t make any difference. To write it out and look at it was as hard as it would be trying to play it without the music. Take your pick.

594.t: Mingus firing the band and the eviction film
594.s: Mingus would fire everyone including himself, and McPherson appeared in a documentary about Mingus's eviction.
594.q: No that was all part of it. No I mean Mingus fired himself. He would get mad at the musicians because they weren’t playing his music right or whatever, and he would fire everybody. The whole band, including him. He would just tell the club owner, you know, this is not right, we’re not playing,…

594.t: Mingus tears up the piano over unpaid money
594.s: At a gangster-owned club Mingus plucked out a piano's strings when unpaid, and the young players were terrified.
594.q: plucks them out with his hands. And so Lonnie and I, we looked at that and here we are, we’ve auditioned to get in this man’s band, and we’re in his band now, and there he is over there tearing the piano up, three hundred pounds. We were like 20 years old, 19, 20. And it was like oh, man, we work…

318.t: The Town Hall big band and Mingus stopping every piece
318.s: He lists the star lineup and tells how Mingus stopped each piece, threatened to quit, and was talked round.
318.q: Yeah Clark and Snooky Young, Ernie Royal, Bernie Glow, trombones Britt Woodman, Butter Jackson — I can’t think of the other trombone player — but all the great guys. In the reed section there was Jerome Richardson, Phil Woods, Pepper Adams, Eric Dolphy, I was there, on and on.

318.t: Clark Terry saves the night with 'In a Mellow Tone'
318.s: Terry starts 'In a Mellow Tone', the audience pulls the curtain back, and the band jams.
318.q: “In a Mellow Tone.” Clark Terry saved us there. Well we had played all night and Mingus’ uncle was there also with a Dixieland band. He did a great job. And then we got back on about 11:00 and did the same thing over and over until the people were getting so disgusted with the band, well we just…

318.t: Mingus's Town Hall concert and the dispute with George Wein
318.s: Mingus asked for him in New York; he describes Mingus declaring the concert an open recording session.
318.q: He felt that he needed me. I knew he didn’t need me as far as the music goes. I mean in certain ways he liked to hear me play then, but he had all the players, he had about 35 musicians or maybe 40, and ten saxophones. So the producer from the record company, United Artists I think, he got on the…

372.s: Granz gave him a weekly advance; Konitz tells of Mingus writing a solo for him and the 1972 big band concert.
372.ch: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
372.q: Just incidentally, Norman was very kind. I’d asked for a weekly stipend as an advance on the royalties and that helped a lot, a hundred dollars a week or whatever he gave me. I always appreciated that.

372.t: The Mingus big band at Philharmonic Hall
372.s: He recalls rehearsals, 'Follow Konitz', Bill Cosby, and a later chat with Mingus.
372.ch: Piano duos, Mingus and the seventies
372.q: I was just invited. Probably Sy Johnson called me. He was kind of in charge of all that. I was more than happy to try it.

372.s: Konitz describes Mingus's support, the Detroit trip, and later hostility.
372.ch: Piano duos, Mingus and the seventies
372.q: Long before that he had asked me to join his small band at the Vanguard. First of all you know he opened the original Half Note and went to the Vanguard and recommended me for the Half Note and I think I was there for thirteen consecutive weeks or something like that. Then he wanted to come back…

228.t: The fight with Mingus in Cleveland
228.s: After McLean gives notice, Mingus punches him and McLean knifes him through his clothes; Mingus fires him and J. R. Monterose.
228.q: Because I had been working with Mingus for a period of time. This particular – he yelled and screamed on the bandstand and gave – shouted orders across the stage and stuff in the middle of your solo. A lot of times he was – anyway, this particular night he was really – so when the set was over and…

228.t: Blakey's anger, the union and Mingus's apology
228.s: Art is outraged when Mingus hits him, the union wants Mingus thrown out, McLean refuses to sign and Mingus later reconciles, writing Portrait of Jackie.
228.q: You mean, how was it, being with him? It was totally different than Charlie Mingus. Art was more like my big brother, my boy. The whole time that I was with him, our two families were connected, in a sense. Art would come down to the house at lot. René and Vernon, Melonae, they knew Art. So Art was…

228.t: Mingus hunts for Jackie and the threatening telegram
228.s: Mingus searches McLean's apartment with Mal Waldron, Dollie turns him away, and a telegram threatens the East River.
228.q: Anyway, but the kicker of this story is that we left for Pittsburgh, me and Donald Byrd, Kenny Drew, Doug Watkins, and Art Blakey, the Messengers. That night, Mingus comes to the gig and Mal said – Mingus said, “Where’s Jackie?” Mal said, “I don’t know, man.” I told Mal I was going. I had to tell…

136.t: Returning to Mingus for the Town Hall concert
136.s: Mingus called her back; a recording turned into a chaotic Town Hall concert with unfinished music and copyists on stage.
136.ch: Lean years, Mingus and Town Hall
136.q: I‟m trying to think what year it was, because after I quit a white lady was the pianist, but then Mingus called me and wanted me to come back. And maybe it was because, he said, “I have a concert,” you know, “I have a recording,” I mean, “I have a recording.” And uh … “So I want you to come back.”…

136.t: Newport, the quintet and Dannie Richmond
136.s: Playing bass on 'Eat That Chicken' at Newport, Lonnie Hillyer and McPherson, Dannie Richmond; she quit for her own music.
136.ch: Lean years, Mingus and Town Hall
136.q: It was really, kind of like that. And uh … then at some point, we were at the Newport festival, but not in Newport, it was Cliff Manor, I think it was called. Cliff, uh … it was more like a protest….

136.s: Mingus recruited her as a new name; rehearsals at his apartment, the Pep's gig and the front line.
136.ch: Lean years, Mingus and Town Hall
136.q: and I didn‟t even know John was there, you know, but he used to come in to, I don‟t know, listen to … well, he used to come in, but anyway…. So, when I was doing that, Mingus came to me and said, “Why don‟t you join my group?” And uh … before that, I must mention about John Lewis, though, because…

367.t: Recording and working with Charles Mingus
367.s: Young says he worked and recorded with Mingus, calls his music difficult, and recalls a big-band piece, perhaps Epitaph or the Town Hall concert.
367.q: Yeah, I knew Charles Mingus. I worked with him quite a bit. I played with him, I did some recordings with him. Mingus had a group in New York, and I worked with that group for a little bit because I was very busy doing other things and I couldn‘t spend too much time with that group because, you…

367.t: Band personnel and Mingus hitting Jimmy Knepper
367.s: They try to name the band's members and Snooky tells of Mingus hitting Jimmy Knepper before a Town Hall concert.
367.q: Benny Powell was in it for a short while. But at first the trumpets, the trombones was Quentin Jackson, and man it’s a shame, my mind is closing up on me. I can’t recall these guys names now.

101.s: Mingus's late music, his tee-shirt announcement and Clark in the Dark, and rescue by Ellington tunes.
101.q: Oh yeah. We did a concert at Town Hall with a big band. We had rehearsed, and he had a lot of new music, but he brought it all too late, and it was impossible for the music to have been played in the short period of time that we had to rehearse it in. He was just going to bulldoze the date anyhow,…

101.t: Mingus nearly chokes Tony Scott on the bus
101.s: An argument over a word on a Southern tour bus leaves Mingus choking Scott.
101.q: Oh yeah. Charles Mingus – Tony, rather, always wanted to play in Ellington’s band, and he always wanted to play Ben Webster’s book in Ellington’s band. So we finally got that going. The first trip was down South. We traveled on the bus. Mingus is sitting – Mingus was with the band then. Mingus is…

28.t: New Year's Eve full dress and Mavouzy's overplaying
28.s: Butler put on full dress at intermission; Mavouzy imitated badly, threatened him, then overplayed Cherokee, and Butler brought the crowd up with Night Train.
28.ch: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
28.q: So one New Year's Eve, at that time on New Year's Eve I always put my full dress on. So Mavouzy--12:00 o'clock--about quarter to 12, I'm going to bring the New Year in in style. So I put the full dress on at intermission. Mavouzy looked, and they said, "Mavouzy, do you see what he's got on?"…

28.t: Mavouzy starts his own band and it collapses
28.s: Mavouzy's rival band on the Grand Boulevard drew people on opening day, but a Jamaican trumpeter cut him with a razor and the audience returned to Butler's.
28.ch: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
28.q: Then we liked to gamble. So people would wait for Mavouzy and give him some of that punch. They'd give him some punch. And Mavouzy would get that punch and go out (inaudible) and get him again. (Inaudible). Then he was so jealous, everytime I talked to a lady, (inaudible).

69.t: Mingus's account of the knife incident, read aloud
69.s: Willard reads Mingus's story from Beneath the Underdog in which Tizol attacks him with a bolo knife at the Apollo and Duke fires him.
69.ch: Pranks, the Mingus fight and Duke's writing
69.q: One of the things I wanted to get your story on was the story, that Charles Mingus tells in his book, his book, Beneath the Underdog when he says he was asked to leave Duke's band because of an incident with a trombone player and an arranger named Juan Tizol. It says, "Tizol wants you to play a…

69.t: Tizol's version of the Mingus confrontation
69.s: Tizol says the story is lies: a quarrel over raising a bass part an octave led to threats, Mingus grabbed an iron bar and was fired.
69.ch: Pranks, the Mingus fight and Duke's writing
69.q: A bunch of lies is right. What really happened; this little piece of music that I wrote for him was nothing that I wrote; I got that from a little legit opera or thing from an a symphony or something, whatever it was.

154.t: The 1962 Mingus Town Hall concert fiasco
154.s: Mingus punched Jimmy Knepper, the rehearsal in front of the audience and the album.
154.q: Yeah they recorded that. But what happened was they pushed the date up a month, which hung him up about writing the music. That’s when he punched Jimmy Knepper in the mouth. And I asked Jimmy how did that happen. He said he was copying music for him and he went up to bring him some music and Mingus…

317.t: The Buffalo arranger's showcase band that fought over a chord
317.s: At a monthly showcase in Buffalo an arranger's dissonant charts caused fights in the band.
317.ch: Power of music and big-band life
317.q: And see that gnarling vibration see, all it matters is that it makes your nerve system catch a good hold of that, and he’d be sitting back like this.

845.t: Charles Mingus: Taj Mahal tubas, big band albums, straw boss
845.s: After Taj Mahal's four-tuba band, he joined Mingus's big band, played on two albums, and became Mingus's straw boss after breaking up a fight.
845.q: Sure. Sure. I got that gig in ’71, 1971. He put together, I think it was some anniversary of the big bands so he put the band back together in 1971. “71? ’72? ‘71 he put the band back together. Because I had just come off the road, that was the January I quit teaching, January of ’72 I quit…

703.t: Jackie McLean stories: ripped pants and the Judson Hall concert
703.s: Jackie's humor and the chase out of Judson Hall after Kennedy's death over missing money.
703.ch: New York, Blue Note and Jackie McLean
703.q: We’re putting our – we’re going to the Port Authority, putting drums and vibes underneath a bus. We get to the club, and Jackie’s not there. The owner of the club says, “Where’s Jackie?” We said he’ll be here soon. Finally, the door opens up, and Jackie comes through the door with his horn. He…

133.t: Mingus's tantrum at the Five Spot and Abbey Lincoln's trio request
133.s: While Walton's trio played opposite Mingus, Mingus wrecked his bass in a fit, and Abbey Lincoln told Max Roach this was the trio she wanted to record with.
133.q: Yeah. Yeah, uh, I think it started when, uh, I told you that uh, I stopped Art Blakey and went into the Five Spot for a long-term engagement and we were opposite, uh, was a trio where we were opposite the Mingus dynasty. I'm not sure he called it the dynasty then, but …

328.s: Mingus heckled at the Vanguard; Hampton later played on a recording with him.
328.q: No, it’s all right. I don’t mind talking about it. It wasn’t very much of an association, but I did – being he was a composer and I was a composer, we had some time that we got to meet. He was always – Mingus was always a strange guy. He came to our performance with the World of Trombones. We…

111.t: Touring with Mingus and Teddy Charles; first Newport Festival
111.s: The quartet played Music Inn, Washington and Newport with Mingus and Teddy Charles constantly arguing.
111.q: That was after that…when he had Dannie Richmond playing with him. At this time he was just playing with trios. He didn’t have his organized band like it is now or like it was later.

464.t: Mingus's unpaid live recording and the television show with written parts
464.s: Mingus secretly recorded the Royce Hall concert and Owens was only paid after Sue Mingus reissued it; the Village Gate TV show with Ralph Ellison had them read written parts.
464.ch: Road bands: Hampton, Crawford and Mingus
464.q: Yeah. We did record in a…. there was one album. It was called “Music That Should Have Been Played In Monterey” or something. We recorded that. It came out, and we never got paid for it. Mingus recorded it secretively. Howard Johnson and I, after we were fired off the bandstand in Los Angeles at…

506.t: The heated argument with Harold Mabern over his notes
506.s: Carter recounts a bandstand fight with a pianist who insisted his chord choices were wrong, later resolved into friendship.
506.q: I don't want to spend a lot of time on that, but really … I guess that was my first real … real … um … real … determining factor on how I felt, how valid my view was on music. Knowing the challenge, what I did up to this point, nobody said, "That's not gonna work." I mean, I played in Miles' band…

102.t: Mingus arrives late and the near fight
102.s: Mingus came in late, shouted about toilet paper, and accused McIntosh of trying to take over when he played piano. McIntosh stood ready to defend himself.
102.ch: New York scene: Mingus, Flanagan, Moody, Quincy
102.q: I started to have an altercation with him once. He always, always came in late. The place is packed every night waiting for him. He is a showman to his heart. He would do something to call attention to himself. One night, he comes in late and goes to the bathroom. Then he yells from the bathroom at…

553.s: How he sat in with Mingus at the Showplace and got hired, the coffin chart, Mingus's assertiveness, and about four months in the band.
553.ch: New York years and Manhattan School
553.q: Okay, well–okay. When I got there in 1960, there was my attitude to go out and play with different peoples, people, so that uh, perhaps, I could get a job, you know...
